scope: Recorded proposal activation on captured live input only, not host execution or strength. Turn-start decisions of two live Deity games of 2026-11-18 (6 players, Continents, Online), neither of which saw a war with a major, and with no denouncement between the seat and any major on the replayed turns (the Kongo game's first is Vietnam's at t117; the Canada game has none): civvis-20261118T045850Z (Kongo beside Canada, Science lane) t10-105, 95 frames (t89 is left out: the live decider read the log at two lengths, so no single prefix is its input), and civvis-20261118T051842Z (the seat is Canada, Diplomatic lane) t25-70, 46 frames. Each case is the exact prefix of events.jsonl the live decider had read (the run's own input capture, checked byte for byte against the log), queried with --turn T --resumed on one ci-profile civvis_orders built from this branch at 8c593da164. Both arms carry the tags the live brain passed as --with (587 and 580), the run's lane and civilization; the on arm adds the gene. The off arm's genome equals the live why.log genome on all 141 frames and its production orders equal the live decider's on 83 of 95 and 43 of 46. A one-frame query has no memory of earlier turns, so the capital and frontier watches read only the soldiers in sight on that frame and arm on fewer frames than the live game did. Kongo: orders differ on 40 frames; the off arm writes 48 journal lines of the peacetime surprise readers (near-rival-deterrence 21 and 2 through its opens-early door, garrison-before-the-surprise 13, capital-archers-before-the-surprise 8, frontier-walls-before-the-surprise 3, capital-walls-before-the-surprise 1), the on arm 2, both near-rival-deterrence against the Aztec at t76-77. Canada: orders differ on 22 frames; the off arm writes 13 such lines (near-rival-deterrence 9, capital-walls-before-the-surprise 4, all against the Maya), the on arm none. Where the off arm's orders hold soldiers and Walls that the on arm's do not (Kongo: 10 Warriors, 10 Archers, 2 Slingers, one of them bought, and 3 Walls; Canada: 5 Archers, a Spearman, a Heavy Chariot, a Swordsman, a Warrior and 1 Walls in production, and two queued-next soldiers), the on arm orders Builders, Traders, Campuses and Monuments (Kongo: Builder 10, Trader 8, one of them bought, Campus 5, Monument 2; Canada: Campus 11, Builder 5), and Masonry is no longer pulled forward on one frame of each game. A soldier still appears in the on arm's changed orders on 10 frames: on 7 the live queue's own nearly finished soldier is finished before the Builder, Trader, Monument or Campus that displaced it, and on 3 it is another city's queued-next pick by the routine picker.
